title: Salesforce to Kestrel migration for Corvid Logistics
request: We are moving off Salesforce at the end of the quarter. Please bring over all accounts, contacts and open opportunities so our account managers can work in Kestrel from day one.

timeline.author: Minh Tran
timeline.text: Kickoff. Scope: Account, Contact, Opportunity (open only). Client exports via Data Loader, we transform and load. Estimate 10 working days.

timeline.author: Tom Becker
timeline.text: first dry run done. 38k rows in, but ~4.1k accounts look like dupes (same company, diff owner/region). do we merge??

timeline.author: Corvid Logistics (ops lead)
timeline.text: Please do NOT merge accounts owned by different regions, they are separate customers for us. Also the Stage picklist has values you don't support, e.g. 'Verbal Yes'.

timeline.author: Minh Tran
timeline.text: Dedupe rule only agreed on day 11: merge on domain + billing country, never across regions. Picklist mapping sheet signed by client. Second dry run needed, plan slips one week.

timeline.author: Minh Tran
timeline.text: Final load OK. 34,112 records after agreed merges. Client sign-off received 2 Apr.

resolution: Migrated 34,112 records after an agreed dedupe rule (domain + billing country, never across regions) and a client-signed picklist mapping. Took two dry runs.
lessons: Agree the dedupe rule in writing before the first dry run. Waiting for it cost us a full week.
Unsupported picklist values always show up. Send the mapping sheet on day 1 and get it signed.
Plan for two dry runs, not one.

artifacts.name: sf-export-mapper.py
artifacts.summary: Transforms Salesforce Data Loader CSVs into Kestrel import format, with picklist mapping from a sheet.

artifacts.name: Migration dedupe checklist v1
artifacts.summary: Questions to agree with the client before deduplicating accounts and contacts.

title: Okta SAML SSO for Lakeview Asset Management
request: Our security team requires all users to sign in through Okta. Can you enable SSO before our next audit?

timeline.author: Daniel Okafor
timeline.text: Sent SAML metadata checklist to client IT (entity ID, ACS URL, NameID = email).

timeline.author: Daniel Okafor
timeline.text: test login fails with 'assertion not yet valid'. their IdP clock is ~3 min ahead

timeline.author: Daniel Okafor
timeline.text: Allowed 5 min clock skew on our side, logins OK. Enforced SSO for all users after client confirmed break-glass admin account.

resolution: Okta SAML enabled with 5 minutes clock skew tolerance and a break-glass admin account kept outside SSO.
lessons: Always keep one break-glass admin outside SSO before enforcing it.
'Assertion not yet valid' is almost always clock skew.

artifacts.name: SAML troubleshooting runbook
artifacts.summary: Common SAML errors (clock skew, wrong ACS URL, NameID format) and how to fix each.

title: Nightly SAP export over SFTP for Orbis Manufacturing
request: Finance needs supplier and contract data from Kestrel in SAP every morning. SAP can pick up a file from SFTP.

timeline.author: Sofia Reyes
timeline.text: Scope: nightly delta export (suppliers, contracts) to client SFTP at 02:00 CET. SAP team owns the import side.

timeline.author: Orbis Manufacturing (SAP team)
timeline.text: Some supplier names are cut off in SAP. Field is max 35 characters on our side.

timeline.author: Sofia Reyes
timeline.text: added truncation + a separate 'long_name' column, sap team ok with it

timeline.author: Priya Nair
timeline.text: heads up: DST switched last night, the 02:00 CET job used local time -> one hour of changes missing from the delta

timeline.author: Sofia Reyes
timeline.text: Rewrote delta window in UTC with a 2h overlap and idempotent upsert keys on the SAP side. Backfilled the missing hour.

resolution: Nightly delta export in UTC with a 2-hour overlap window and idempotent keys, plus a long_name column for SAP's 35-character limit.
lessons: Never schedule deltas in local time. Use UTC and an overlap window, the target must upsert idempotently.
Ask for the target system's field length limits during mapping, not after go-live.
Run a test across a DST change if the project spans March/October.

artifacts.name: SFTP sync runbook
artifacts.summary: How to set up, monitor and backfill a nightly SFTP delta export.

artifacts.name: SAP field mapping sheet
artifacts.summary: Kestrel to SAP field mapping including length limits.

title: Quarterly investor report export for Riverside Wealth

timeline.author: Linh Pham

timeline.author: Linh Pham

resolution: PDF template rebuilt from the client's previous real report, with per-fund fee breakdown and compliance footer.
lessons: For any report or document request, ask for a real sample of the current output before building anything.

artifacts.summary: Quarterly investor statement with per-fund fees and configurable compliance footer.

artifacts.summary: Excel import template with dropdown validation and fixed date formats.

title: Month-end dashboard slowness escalated by Meridian Health Partners
request: Our finance dashboard takes more than 30 seconds to load at month-end. Our CFO cannot close the books. This needs to be fixed now.

timeline.author: Meridian Health Partners (CFO office)
timeline.text: Escalating: dashboard unusable for the third month in a row. We need a named owner and daily updates.

timeline.author: Daniel Okafor
timeline.text: can't reproduce today, loads in 2s. only slow at month-end??

timeline.author: Priya Nair
timeline.text: Found it: the dashboard filters on custom field 'cost_center' (not indexed) AND their month-end batch import of 60k invoices runs at the same time.

timeline.author: Daniel Okafor
timeline.text: Index added on cost_center. Asked client to move batch import to 01:00. Daily status emails sent since 30 May.

timeline.author: Meridian Health Partners (CFO office)
timeline.text: Month-end close went fine, dashboard loads in 3 seconds. Thanks for the daily updates.

resolution: Indexed the custom filter field and moved the client's month-end batch import out of business hours. Daily status emails during the escalation.
lessons: Ask WHEN it is slow, not just what. Month-end slowness usually means a competing batch job.
Check filters on custom fields first: they are not indexed by default.
In an escalation, send a daily update even when there is no news. The client said it mattered most.

artifacts.name: Performance triage checklist
artifacts.summary: Questions and queries to run when a client reports slowness.

title: Azure AD SSO and SCIM provisioning for Tidewater Insurance
request: We need SSO with Azure AD and automatic user provisioning and deprovisioning, so leavers lose access the same day.

timeline.author: Sofia Reyes
timeline.text: SAML + SCIM via Azure AD enterprise app. Needs Global Admin consent on client side.

timeline.author: Sofia Reyes
timeline.text: still no admin consent. our contact is in HR, not IT. lost a week

timeline.author: Tidewater Insurance (IT security)
timeline.text: In testing, a disabled user is still in the 'Claims' group in Kestrel. That fails our leaver policy.

timeline.author: Sofia Reyes
timeline.text: Known bug ENG-882: SCIM deprovision deactivates the user but leaves group memberships. Fixed in release 4.12. Client tenant upgraded early.

timeline.author: Daniel Okafor
timeline.text: Department attribute mapped to Kestrel teams. Leaver test passed with IT security watching.

resolution: Azure AD SAML + SCIM live after early upgrade to release 4.12 (fix for ENG-882) and a witnessed leaver test.
lessons: Get the client's IT admin (the person who can grant consent) named at kickoff. Business contacts cannot do it.
Test deprovisioning explicitly, including group memberships. Security teams will.
SCIM needs release 4.12 or later.

artifacts.name: Azure AD SCIM setup guide
artifacts.summary: Step-by-step Azure AD enterprise app setup, attribute mapping and leaver test script.

title: Bulk investor onboarding with e-sign templates for Sable Ventures
request: We are closing a new fund and need to onboard about 3,000 investors, each signing a subscription agreement in Kestrel.

timeline.author: Marco Bianchi
timeline.text: Tag signature/date/initial fields on the subscription agreement PDF, then bulk invite 3,000 investors.

timeline.author: Sable Ventures (legal counsel)
timeline.text: Attached is the final version of the agreement, we added two pages on side letters.

timeline.author: Marco Bianchi
timeline.text: new pdf shifts every page after p.12, all my tags are off. retagging 41 fields

timeline.author: Marco Bianchi
timeline.text: Retagged and re-tested with 5 internal signers before the bulk invite. Asked legal to confirm this is FINAL in writing.

resolution: Template retagged on the final PDF, tested with 5 internal signers, then 3,000 invites sent in batches of 500.
lessons: Freeze the document version in writing before tagging fields. Any late page change breaks every tag after it.
Test with a few internal signers before a bulk invite.
Send bulk invites in batches of 500 to keep bounce handling manageable.

artifacts.name: E-sign template tagging checklist
artifacts.summary: Document freeze, field tagging and signer test steps before a bulk e-sign campaign.

title: HubSpot to Kestrel migration for Saffron Retail Group
request: Migrate our CRM from HubSpot: companies, contacts, deals and notes. We want to switch off HubSpot in six weeks.

timeline.author: Tom Becker
timeline.text: Export through HubSpot API. Objects: companies, contacts, deals, notes. Estimate 15 days.

timeline.author: Tom Becker
timeline.text: hubspot api throttling us hard (429s). full export would take ~5 days at this rate

timeline.author: Saffron Retail Group (CRM manager)
timeline.text: Where are the attachments? Our team relies on the contracts attached to deals. About 40 GB.

timeline.author: Linh Pham
timeline.text: Attachments were never in the written scope. Agreed change request: +6 days.

timeline.author: Tom Becker
timeline.text: Switched to incremental export by last-modified date with exponential backoff. Final delta on cutover night took 40 minutes.

resolution: Incremental export by last-modified date with backoff, plus attachments added via a change request. 120k records and 40 GB of files.
lessons: Ask explicitly about attachments and files in the scope questionnaire.
Expect API rate limits on SaaS CRMs: export incrementally by last-modified date and keep the final delta small.
Write scope down per object. 'Migrate our CRM' means different things to everyone.

artifacts.name: hubspot-incremental-export.js
artifacts.summary: Incremental HubSpot export by last-modified date with exponential backoff on 429s.

artifacts.name: Migration scope questionnaire
artifacts.summary: Per-object scope questions including attachments, history and inactive records.

title: Two-way Salesforce sync for Alder & Finch Capital
request: Our sales team stays in Salesforce, operations work in Kestrel. Contacts and accounts must stay in sync both ways.

timeline.author: Priya Nair
timeline.text: Two-way sync for Account and Contact. Rule agreed: last write wins, except owner field always from Salesforce.

timeline.author: Sofia Reyes
timeline.text: we have a ping-pong: update in SF -> we write -> SF trigger fires -> writes back. infinite loop on 30 records

timeline.author: Priya Nair
timeline.text: Added origin flag + 'last synced hash' so we skip echoes of our own writes. Pattern documented.

resolution: Two-way sync with an origin flag and last-synced hash to stop echo loops, and an agreed per-field conflict rule.
lessons: Every two-way sync needs echo protection from day one (origin flag + hash).
Agree conflict rules per field with the client, in writing.

artifacts.name: Sync loop guard pattern
artifacts.summary: Design note on origin flags and hashes to prevent two-way sync loops.

timeline.author: Tom Becker
timeline.text: 2M rows initial load, then daily deltas. Their team signed the schema doc on day 1, no surprises.

resolution: Daily delta export to Snowflake against a schema the client's data team signed on day 1.
lessons: With data teams, sign the schema doc on day 1. It removed every later question.

artifacts.name: Warehouse export config template
artifacts.summary: Config and schema doc template for scheduled warehouse exports (Snowflake, BigQuery).

title: Dynamics 365 migration with Vietnamese and Japanese data for Eastwind Shipping
request: Move our customer and contract records from Dynamics 365 into Kestrel. Our offices are in Singapore, Ho Chi Minh City and Osaka.

timeline.author: Minh Tran
timeline.text: Dynamics export to CSV by client IT, we transform with the usual mapper. Estimate 12 days.

timeline.author: Eastwind Shipping (compliance)
timeline.text: Reminder: our data must be processed and stored in Singapore only.

timeline.author: Minh Tran
timeline.text: we're on the US tenant by default, need to redo env in SG region. +3 days

timeline.author: Eastwind Shipping (HCMC office)
timeline.text: Customer names in Vietnamese are broken after go-live, e.g. 'CÃ´ng ty' instead of 'Công ty'. Japanese names in Osaka are question marks. This is unacceptable.

timeline.author: Minh Tran
timeline.text: Root cause: client exported CSV in Windows-1252, not UTF-8. Our load did not validate encoding. ~18k records affected. Re-export and re-import planned.

timeline.author: Tom Becker
timeline.text: Wrote encoding-check.py: flags mojibake patterns before load. Re-import done, native speakers in HCMC and Osaka checked 200 samples each.

resolution: Rebuilt in the Singapore region, then a full re-import from UTF-8 exports after mojibake broke ~18k Vietnamese and Japanese records. Validated by native speakers.
lessons: Force UTF-8 exports and run encoding-check.py before ANY load with non-English data.
Have a native speaker check a sample of each language before go-live, not after.
Check data residency at kickoff. Moving to another region later cost 3 days.

artifacts.name: encoding-check.py
artifacts.summary: Detects mojibake and wrong encodings in CSV files before load (Vietnamese, Japanese, accented Latin).

artifacts.name: APAC residency checklist
artifacts.summary: Which region/tenant to use for APAC clients and what to confirm at kickoff.

title: Okta SCIM provisioning for Northgate Credit Union
request: We already use Okta SSO with you. Now we want Okta to create and remove users automatically.

timeline.author: Daniel Okafor
timeline.text: Enable SCIM on existing Okta app. Release 4.15, so ENG-882 not a concern.

timeline.author: An Nguyen
timeline.text: ~140 duplicate users appeared. JIT provisioning was still on, SCIM created a second account when emails differed in case

timeline.author: Daniel Okafor

resolution: JIT disabled, duplicates merged by lower-cased email, clashing push groups renamed. Then SCIM enabled cleanly.
lessons: Disable JIT provisioning before enabling SCIM, and normalise existing users' emails to lower case first.
Check Okta push group names against existing Kestrel team names before the first push.
